title: Full linear span does not settle sparse representability
summary: The disjoint packet dictionary spans its whole 25-dimensional common space and the target has a nine-packet expression, yet no two-packet expression exists.
content: The disjoint packet dictionary spans its whole 25-dimensional common space and the target has a nine-packet expression, yet no two-packet expression exists. This is an exact reason to stop searching for a linear separating functional for that obstruction. Nine is an upper bound, not a claimed minimum.
whenToUse: Checking whether a linear separating functional can possibly certify a sparse-representation obstruction.
limitations: This is a dictionary-specific finite example. Nine is an upper bound on packet count, not an established minimum.
